_readme: Themed puzzles. This file is the ONLY place a theme is authored — the
generator merges it over the generated set, so an editor never touches code.
A theme claims a base word. Claimed bases are generated FIRST and win their
anagram slot, so a claim reliably lands. Clues written here override the
auto-generated Webster ones; anything not overridden falls back, so a theme
Clue rules, enforced by the build (it prints what it rejected and why):
- never contain the answer or a 4+ character stem of it
- no two rows in a puzzle may pose the same question
VOICE NOTE: these are a first draft written to prove the pipeline and give
an editor something to react to. They should be revised by someone with

VOICE NOTE: specific over general. A clue should name a thing you can picture — a red cup, a thick envelope, the chair by the window — not gesture at a mood. Generic warmth reads as an outsider being careful.

themes.name: The Cookout
themes.blurb: Paper plates, folding chairs, somebody's uncle on the grill.

themes.name: 90s R&B
themes.blurb: Slow jams, harmonies, and a CD case in the car door.

themes.name: Sitcom Sunday
themes.blurb: Reruns, laugh tracks, and everybody's living room.

themes.name: HBCU
themes.blurb: The yard, the band, the homecoming.

themes.name: Barbershop
themes.blurb: The chair, the clippers, and the argument already in progress.

themes.name: In the Kitchen
themes.blurb: The pan that is only hers, an oven that runs fifty hot, and a recipe that lives nowhere but her hands.

themes.name: Sunday Dinner
themes.blurb: Second pew, white gloves, and the pot roast that went in before service.

themes.name: Fish Fry
themes.blurb: Twelve dollars, two sides, and the cash box she does not hand to anybody.

themes.name: Family Reunion
themes.blurb: Matching shirts, a hotel block, a printed program, and the committee that made it happen.

themes.name: The Beauty Shop
themes.blurb: Twenty-two bottles, a standing Saturday, and an appointment that takes all day.

themes.name: The Card Table
themes.blurb: Four chairs, a bid you have to make, and a score kept on the back of an envelope.

themes.name: Sunday Service
themes.blurb: The organ, the usher's white glove, and the front row that decides everything.

themes.name: Homecoming Weekend
themes.blurb: A hotel sold out since March, a lot full by Thursday, and a game nobody watches past the half.

themes.name: The Line Forms
themes.blurb: Nobody announced it — by the second verse there are four rows and your aunt is in front.

themes.name: The Nineteenth
themes.blurb: A paper read out loud on a Galveston balcony, two and a half years late.

clues.cousin: Not your mother's sister's kid. Nobody can chart it and nobody asks.
clues.icons: Three framed in the hallway: Martin, Kennedy, and your grandmother.
clues.coins: Dug out the couch when you heard the truck turn onto the next street.
clues.sun: Still all the way up at eight o'clock and nobody's going inside.
clues.son: He fixed a plate, ate standing up, and got told to sit down twice.
clues.cons: Listed out by whoever is angling not to host it next year.

clues.vocals: What you rewound the tape for, right before the ad libs start.
clues.sol: The fifth note. What the choir director hums to start you off.
clues.cola: Dark, sweet, over ice, in a red cup, on a folding table.
clues.also: In addition. What the liner notes say before four more names.
clues.coals: Still glowing at nine, long after everybody has eaten.
clues.oval: The shape of the track, and of the platter that comes out twice a year.

clues.sample: Somebody else's four bars, looped until they belong to you.
clues.psalm: Where the loop came from before it was a loop. Sunday, first.
clues.slam: A door, a dunk, or a poem delivered like it owes you money.
clues.plea: The bridge, on both knees, asking her to pick up the phone.
clues.leaps: What the chorus does after the verse spent a whole minute holding back.
clues.ample: More than enough. The amount she cooked for six people.

clues.sitcom: Twenty-two minutes, one couch, everything fixed before the credits.
clues.sit: What the whole family did at 8pm, same night, same room, every week.
clues.stoic: Unbothered on purpose. The father, every episode, same chair.
clues.most: The greatest share. What the youngest swears the oldest always gets.
clues.cost: What the very special episode was about, right before the hug.
clues.mist: What sits on a cold glass on the porch in July.

clues.laughs: Canned, and always about half a second early.
clues.hugs: How every episode lands once the music goes soft.
clues.gals: What the announcer called them in 1994 and nobody blinked.
clues.lash: To tie down tight — or the strip somebody spent forty minutes on.
clues.gush: To pour praise so thick the person has to look at the floor.

clues.campus: The Yard. The band cuts through and everybody has somewhere to be.
clues.camps: August. A week before anybody else arrives, learning the drill.
clues.caps: Thrown straight up on the lawn, and not all of them come back down.
clues.maps: Useless by October. You cut the same diagonal as everyone else.
clues.scam: The table by the union with the free t-shirt and the credit form.
clues.cap: Worn backwards, or what somebody calls your story when it stretches.

clues.alumni: Graduated in '04, still knows every word of the fight song.
clues.mail: The thick envelope. You knew from the weight before you opened it.
clues.main: The one street everybody parks along the whole homecoming weekend.
clues.aim: What the guidance counselor asked about and you answered too small.
clues.nail: To land it exactly, the way the drumline hits the downbeat.
clues.man: What your father called you the first time he meant it.

clues.chairs: Four of them, and you know whose is whose before anybody sits.
clues.hair: What the cape catches, and what you find on your collar at dinner.
clues.cash: The sign on the mirror has said this since 1997. No, not that app.
clues.arch: The curve he checks twice before the razor goes near your eyebrow.
clues.scar: The small one from the time you moved. He still brings it up.
clues.crash: To come in with no appointment and hope somebody cancels.

clues.shaved: Taken to the skin with a straight blade and zero hesitation.
clues.shave: Hot towel first, then the neck, then the part you can't see.
clues.heads: Every one turns when the door opens. Every single time.
clues.shade: Somewhere cool to stand — or what she just threw, smiling.
clues.save: What the line-up did for that photo you almost didn't take.
clues.hades: The Greek underworld, and the god who runs it, same name.

clues.faucet: Where the water comes out, and where the dishes stack up under it.
clues.cafe: You ordered one coffee and stayed a solid two hours past that.
clues.feta: White, salty, crumbles over everything in the summer.
clues.tea: Poured sweet by the pitcher — or what somebody is about to spill.
clues.eat: What she says four times before anybody actually sits down.
clues.cut: Into the cake, and somebody films it.

clues.deacon: Dark suit, first pew, and he starts the hymn before the organ finds the key.
clues.ocean: Where the baptizing happened before there was a pool built in up front.
clues.cane: Hooked over the back of the pew in front of her, where she can reach it.
clues.once: How many times the announcements were meant to be read out this morning.
clues.done: What he is not, no matter how many times he has said in closing.
clues.code: The dress kind. Unwritten, never posted, and enforced by everybody's mother.

clues.sermon: Twenty minutes on paper. Forty-five once the organ starts up behind him.
clues.snore: The man three pews back, and his wife's elbow arriving right on schedule.
clues.nose: The usher's, wrinkled, at the child who walked in with a bag of chips.
clues.more: What the choir gives the last verse when nobody wants to sit back down.
clues.ones: Folded small inside a glove, counted twice before the plate comes around.
clues.morn: The six o'clock service, for people who like the building half empty.

clues.gospel: They come in on the second verse and the whole building gets to its feet.
clues.pose: How you sat for the picture in the fellowship hall: hands folded, hat on.
clues.sole: The bottom of the shoe she wore through walking that aisle every Sunday.
clues.legs: The folding table has four, and one of them has been short since 1998.
clues.lose: What you do with the count of how many times he has said in closing.
clues.goes: What the organ does underneath him, low, long before anybody says amen.

clues.anthem: Lift Every Voice. The second verse, and your grandmother knows it cold.
clues.amen: Said early, by one man in the back, and it is not a question he is asking.
clues.meant: What the whole row decided that line was about, and it was about them.
clues.name: On the back of the funeral home fan, with a phone number underneath it.
clues.meat: Sunday's is a roast. Wednesday's is whatever is left of Sunday's.
clues.math: What the ushers do in the back with the count, twice, before it is read.

clues.organs: The Hammond up front, and the man who has been sitting at it since 1978.
clues.organ: Two speakers, one bench, and a sound the piano has never once matched.
clues.sang: What she did at one funeral, and got asked at every funeral after that.
clues.song: Started in the back of the room before the musicians had found the key.
clues.rags: The bag of them under the fellowship hall sink, cut from old choir robes.
clues.soar: What the last note does while the drummer holds everything else down.

clues.mother: White dress, second pew from the front, and the last word on everything.
clues.other: The one nobody sits in. It is hers, and it has been hers since 1991.
clues.home: What she calls going, and it is not the house she means.
clues.hero: Not the word she would use. She would say he was raised right, and stop.
clues.moth: Comes out of the closet with the suit you only wear twice a year.
clues.term: How long she has served on the usher board, and nobody has ever counted.

clues.mashed: Real potatoes, the whole afternoon, and the mixer stays in the cabinet.
clues.shade: On the porch after the meal, or what your cousin just quietly threw.
clues.heads: Bowed, all of them, before one fork is allowed to touch one plate.
clues.made: From scratch, and she will say it that way while you are eating it.
clues.mesh: The screen door that slams no matter how gently you think you closed it.
clues.shed: Where the extra folding chairs get carried back to when plates are cleared.

clues.prayed: Over the food, over the drive home, and over a name nobody said out loud.
clues.pray: What she told you to do about it, and it was not the answer you came for.
clues.ready: What the table is, twenty minutes before anybody will sit down at it.
clues.year: How long since the whole family was in this room at the same time.
clues.read: The scripture, by whichever grandchild can be made to stand up front.
clues.yard: Where the children are sent so the grown folks can talk about the will.

clues.player: Six discs in the changer, and he tells you which one before he pulls off.
clues.relay: One car hands it to the next at the light: same station, same song.
clues.pearl: One on a chain, over the collarbone, in the portrait from '96.
clues.layer: The jacket he keeps on all night in August because of the shirt under it.
clues.plea: The bridge, on both knees, asking her to pick up the phone.
clues.pale: The light off the dashboard clock, the only thing on at two in the morning.

clues.singer: One mic, one stool, and a sweater she is not taking off.
clues.reign: Four years where nothing else got played after midnight.
clues.rinse: What the dishes get during the slow one, so nobody has to talk.
clues.resin: What the tree leaves on the hood when you park under it all night.
clues.grin: What he did in the doorway when the man on air read his name out.
clues.sign: Two fingers out the window, one horn tap, and he's gone.

clues.slower: What he asked for at the booth, and half the floor sat down.
clues.lower: What his hand did to the dial once it stopped being about anybody else.
clues.swore: On the porch at seventeen, that this one was going to be permanent.
clues.worse: The second tape she made him, and it still lives in the car door.
clues.rose: One, still in the gas station plastic, handed over at 11:40.
clues.wore: The velour set, in the mall portrait, with the laser background.

clues.chorus: Everybody in the car comes in, and nobody was invited.
clues.hours: Ten to two. The format, and the reason the phone lines opened.
clues.rush: What the drive home stopped being once the slow set started.
clues.sour: Her face when he said the tape was for somebody at work.
clues.such: The word the man on air leaned on before reading the dedication.
clues.ouch: The high note he tried in the passenger seat and did not reach.

clues.dances: He knows two, and he does both at every single reception.
clues.dance: Arms on the shoulders, four inches of daylight, chaperone watching.
clues.cased: The whole rack, twice, before spending the eight dollars.
clues.scan: Down the spine of the shelf, hunting the one with the sticker.
clues.sand: Still in the floor mats in November, from one July weekend.
clues.cane: Hooked on the back of the folding chair, and he is still moving.

clues.minute: How long the intro ran before anybody sang a single word.
clues.mute: Hit the second his mother came into the room.
clues.time: What the ad libs were stealing, and nobody minded a bit.
clues.tune: What he did to the truck radio, two fingers, eyes still on the road.
clues.untie: The ribbon on the tape she wrapped like it was a real gift.
clues.unite: What the last chorus does to a room that spent all night apart.

clues.candle: Two on the table and the overhead off. He tried, and it worked.
clues.clean: The car, Saturday morning, before anybody knew who was riding in it.
clues.laced: White ones, done twice, tucked in, before the doorbell went.
clues.dance: Arms on the shoulders and a chaperone counting the daylight.
clues.land: What the run does at the end, exactly where it was supposed to.
clues.lace: Down the front of the church dress, and it itched all service.

clues.trunks: On the shower rod since June and still not dry.
clues.trunk: Popped in the lot so the whole parking row could hear it.
clues.turns: Three extra ones around the block so the song could finish.
clues.stunk: The first mix, and he played it for you anyway.
clues.rust: Under the wheel well, so he parks with the good side facing you.
clues.nuts: Hot, in a paper cone, a dollar, outside before doors.

clues.hearts: Drawn in the margin of a tracklist somebody wrote out by hand.
clues.heart: What the ad lib says is broken, in a key nobody else can reach.
clues.share: One set of headphones, one bus seat, one side each.
clues.earth: What the bass in the back moves, two cars over at the light.
clues.hates: What she says about the song, and not what she does when it comes on.
clues.stare: Held across the room for the length of one whole verse.

clues.pagers: Clipped to the belt, and 07734 was the entire message.
clues.pages: The liner notes, unfolded all the way across the passenger seat.
clues.gears: Second, then third, right as the drums come in.
clues.rages: What the second verse does after the first one spent itself begging.
clues.sage: Burning in a shell on the sill before she would let anybody in.
clues.ears: Ringing after, because the back of the car did most of the work.

clues.cruise: Speed limit exactly, windows down, nowhere in particular to be.
clues.curse: Bleeped out on the radio cut, and everybody says it anyway.
clues.cures: What the man at midnight promised the next record would do.
clues.cries: Twice on the bridge, once more on the way to work on Monday.
clues.sure: What she said, meaning the opposite, when he asked about the tape.
clues.rise: What the key does one step for the last chorus, and you feel it.

clues.sauced: Yellow, not red. Anybody who tells you different is from another state.
clues.sauce: The gallon jug rode down in the floorboard because the store kind is wrong.
clues.cause: The reason given for driving four hours. The real one is nobody's seen anybody.
clues.case: A flat of red drink under the folding table, still in the cardboard.
clues.used: The foil pans everybody swore they would wash and bring back.
clues.aces: What your uncle claims he was holding, three hands after the deal.

clues.smoker: Welded out of a drum by a cousin. It has a name and its own trailer hitch.
clues.smoke: Thin and blue is right. Thick and white means somebody opened the lid.
clues.some: How much rice is left after the first pass. Enough to argue about.
clues.more: What the man with the tongs says after you already told him you were full.
clues.sore: Your back the next morning, from the folding chair with the busted strap.
clues.rose: What the canopy did at six in the morning: four men, one set of directions.

clues.uncles: Two by blood, three by proximity, and one nobody has ever been able to place.
clues.uncle: Owns the pit. Did not buy the meat, will not clean it, accepts the credit.
clues.clues: You get none. You just know which cooler in the carport is not for you.
clues.lens: He has had the camcorder up since noon and nobody has asked him to stop.
clues.sun: Behind the pines by nine, which is when the bug spray comes out of the truck.
clues.use: What the good pan is not for. That one goes to church and comes back.

clues.auntie: Not blood. Still, do not let her hear you say her first name by itself.
clues.aunt: Came in with a covered dish and a list of who did not speak to her last year.
clues.tuna: Somebody always brings it, nobody claims it, and the bowl still comes back empty.
clues.untie: What you do to the apron string before she will let you hug her.
clues.unit: The window kind, dripping in the flower bed, cooling the one room everybody wants.
clues.tune: Came on and three generations stood up without anybody being asked.

clues.hosted: You said yes to it back in February. It is July now and ninety people are coming.
clues.host: The only one holding a plate the whole afternoon and never once sitting down.
clues.hose: Green, coiled by the spigot, and the only air conditioning the kids get.
clues.shoe: Left by the back steps. Its match is somewhere out in the yard.
clues.shot: The group picture, taken twice, because Granddaddy blinked the first time.
clues.shed: Where the extra chairs live, behind the mower and the Christmas box.

clues.shrimp: Heads on, in the pot with corn and sausage, poured out onto newspaper.
clues.ship: What the box of pecans does every December, taped shut and addressed by hand.
clues.hips: What the electric slide is hard on once you are past about fifty.
clues.prim: How the church ladies sit down, and how they do not eat.
clues.rips: What the paper plate does the second the second helping lands on it.
clues.rim: Salt around the glass, and the part of the pot you grab with a towel.

clues.boiled: Peanuts in a wet paper bag, bought off a truck at the county line, still hot.
clues.boil: The pot out on the propane burner, because it will never fit on the stove.
clues.oiled: The grates, with half an onion on a fork, before anything touches them.
clues.idle: Two men standing over the pit doing nothing at all, and doing it seriously.
clues.lobe: Where the good earrings go, and they go in only after the cooking is done.
clues.deli: The plastic tub the potato salad arrived in. It has never fooled anybody.

clues.melons: Cut over the sink at ten in the morning so they are cold by two.
clues.melon: One end sweeter than the other, and every child in the yard knows which end.
clues.lemon: Halved into the tea pitcher, then rubbed on your hands after you clean fish.
clues.solemn: How the blessing goes, right up until somebody's phone starts ringing.
clues.mole: The one on her cheek that half the women in this family got a version of.
clues.nose: Tells you the pit is ready from three houses down the street.

clues.spiced: The rub went on last night, which is why nobody could get into the fridge.
clues.spice: The tin with no label on it that she will not let you take a picture of.
clues.dice: What he does to the onion, small, so the children cannot see it and refuse.
clues.iced: Sweet enough to stand a spoon in, in the yellow cooler with the spout.
clues.side: There are eleven of them and exactly one kind of meat left on the table.
clues.pies: Sweet potato, two of them, and one is already spoken for by name.

clues.basket: Lined with a dish towel, and the rolls under it are still warm at four.
clues.bakes: She does it Saturday night so that Sunday is nothing but reheating.
clues.beast: On the pit since two in the morning, and two men slept in chairs beside it.
clues.steak: Not what is on this grill. Somebody brought it anyway and got looked at.
clues.seat: There are not enough. The children eat standing up and think that is normal.
clues.task: Yours is ice. It is always ice, and you will be sent back out for more.

clues.gravel: The driveway. You hear every car that turns in before you ever see it.
clues.grave: He drives out there with flowers Sunday morning before he comes to eat.
clues.large: The size of the foil pan, and the number of folks who said they were coming.
clues.glare: What she sends across the yard, and it still works from forty feet away.
clues.gavel: Whoever brought one to the reunion meeting was serious, and got laughed at.
clues.gear: Tongs, thermometer, spray bottle. Nobody else is permitted to touch any of it.

clues.phrase: Two words, said the same way every week, and the studio room detonates.
clues.share: What the last piece of cake becomes when a fourth cousin walks in.
clues.sharp: Pressed, creased, and photographed on the stairs before the dance.
clues.hears: What the whole block does when the front door slams at midnight.
clues.spare: The key under the mat, and the room the cousin from Philadelphia gets.
clues.shape: What he swears he is still in, right before he takes the stairs too fast.

clues.taping: Done in front of an audience that laughed for real before the machine did.
clues.paint: The wall behind the couch, done over one weekend and never mentioned again.
clues.giant: What the little brother is now, six inches over everybody, in one summer.
clues.pain: What he claims his back is in whenever there are groceries in the car.
clues.gain: What the bathroom scale reports after two weeks of her cooking.
clues.pint: What the ice cream comes in, and it is not going back in the freezer full.

clues.dozens: Your-mama jokes, escalating, a circle forming, and somebody keeping score.
clues.nose: How the pot finds you from the top of the stairs before anybody calls you.
clues.zones: What he does out in the recliner nine minutes into the evening news.
clues.ones: Counted out of a birthday card by the smallest cousin, twice, out loud.
clues.send: What she does to you upstairs, mid-sentence, the second company arrives.
clues.done: What the plate is when the fork gets set down at that particular angle.

clues.cameos: The singing group turns up at the school dance in full outfits, for no reason.
clues.same: What everybody's outfit is in the reunion picture, and it was not optional.
clues.scam: The uncle's business idea, explained on a napkin, at the kitchen table.
clues.comes: What the whole block does out onto the porch when the tour bus pulls up.
clues.seam: Where the church suit finally gave up, halfway through the second sermon.
clues.aces: What the card table claims somebody has, right before the argument.

clues.movers: Two men, a truck, and a couch that does not fit the new building's elevator.
clues.more: What the new apartment has of everything, including stairs nobody needed.
clues.sore: What the back is after eleven floors and a box marked FRAGILE that wasn't.
clues.rose: Cut from the old yard, riding up front in a coffee can with foil on top.
clues.some: How much of the old furniture makes the trip. The rest goes to the church.
clues.moves: What the reception floor calls for, and he has exactly two of them.

clues.mantel: Where the school portraits sit in order, and the bad one is still up there.
clues.metal: The folding chair out of the hall closet when the cousins come over.
clues.name: What she uses all three of when you are already in trouble.
clues.meant: What she says the tone did, and you both know exactly what it did.
clues.late: What you are, and the porch light was already on when you turned the corner.
clues.team: What the whole front room becomes at eight o'clock on a Sunday in January.

clues.pastor: Coming for dinner, so the good plates came out of the cabinet yesterday.
clues.roast: In the oven since before service started, on a timer she does not trust.
clues.sport: What the coat is called, and it is the only one he owns with a lining.
clues.oats: Breakfast on a school morning, and there is no negotiating about it.
clues.trap: What the boy walked straight into, answering one question too many.
clues.star: What the first-Sunday soloist becomes for exactly four minutes.

clues.cosign: To put your name behind his story, in front of his mother, and just hope.
clues.sign: Taped inside the front door, in her handwriting, listing what you will not do.
clues.song: Comes on, and the whole room changes key, including the man in the chair.
clues.icon: The photo over the doorway, up there since before you were born.
clues.con: What the smallest one runs on the babysitter, and it works every time.
clues.coin: Flipped for the last piece, and somebody always calls it in the air.

clues.single: One apartment, four women, and a phone cord stretched into the hallway.
clues.lines: What the phone has two of, and one belongs to the answering machine.
clues.lens: What the boyfriend brings, then takes forty pictures of the brunch table.
clues.legs: What the heels are for, and they come off the second the door shuts.
clues.gels: Lays the edges before you leave, and one jar serves the whole apartment.
clues.sing: What she does over the record, louder than the record, every Saturday.

clues.credit: The couch was bought on it, and the payment book lives in the kitchen drawer.
clues.diet: Started on the first of the month, over by the time the fry pan comes out.
clues.tired: What he is, and he announces it before he gets the second boot off.
clues.tried: What he swears he did, and the folded paper from school says otherwise.
clues.rice: In the pot before anything else, and always more than six people need.
clues.iced: The tea, by the pitcher, sweet enough to hold a spoon upright.

clues.grades: The school envelope, opened at the table, in front of every single person.
clues.read: What she does to the whole card, twice, before she says one word.
clues.sage: The green in the dressing, and only she is allowed to measure it.
clues.gear: The bag by the door, packed last night, because there is no second trip.
clues.dare: What the look across the table is, and nobody at that table takes it.
clues.drag: What the walk from the bus stop becomes with that envelope in your bag.

clues.father: Loud, present, filling the doorway, asking who exactly told you that.
clues.heart: What she says he has, right after telling him to lower his voice.
clues.after: When the real talk happens: everybody upstairs, kitchen light only.
clues.heat: What the kitchen has in August, because the window unit is in the bedroom.
clues.fare: The exact change he counts into your hand before you get on the bus.
clues.tear: What she wipes off before she turns around, and nobody in the room saw it.

clues.raised: The whole point of the night. Twenty-two hundred by nine, announced Sunday morning.
clues.aside: Where the pastor's box gets set, foil on top, so nobody sells it out from under him.
clues.ideas: The suggestion on the wall said add fried chicken. The committee voted it down.
clues.dries: What the fish does on a rack of newspaper for ninety seconds. No longer.
clues.arise: To come up, the way the question of charging fourteen does at every meeting.
clues.raid: What the kids do to the bread bag while nobody is watching the side table.

clues.filets: Whiting, cut thin, three to a box, because croaker takes too long to cook.
clues.left: By seven there is only slaw. The sign gets flipped and the basement door locked.
clues.list: Taped to the wall downstairs: who fries, who bags, who counts. She wrote it.
clues.fist: What the man in front of you makes when they say the last box is already sold.
clues.stifle: To hold something back, the way the screen door fails to hold back the smell.

clues.fast: The one-handed shuffle she does while telling a story about her sister.
clues.fate: Whatever the cut hands you. You bid it anyway and say nothing.
clues.seat: The one against the wall. His since 1996, and no, you cannot have it.

clues.calmed: It took two rounds and a fresh glass of ice water after the renege argument.
clues.medal: There is no trophy here. There is a name on the back of an envelope.
clues.made: Bid four, took four. Nothing extra, nothing owed to anybody.
clues.calm: How she stays while he is up out of his chair about a card he threw himself.
clues.clam: What he goes quiet as, the second he works out that he is set.
clues.lame: The excuse about the light, the chair, the deck. Heard it all before.

clues.scaled: The bid climbed four, five, six, because neither side would back down.
clues.scale: What the whole night is measured on: five hundred, and not one point more.
clues.case: The little box the deck came in, gone since the second week.
clues.seal: To close it out — the last book taken quietly with a two.
clues.laced: How she talks: sweet on top, something else underneath it.
clues.ales: Bottles sweating on the counter. Never, ever set on the table itself.

clues.packed: Six chairs in a kitchen corner built for four, and nobody minds.
clues.aced: Cut clean by the highest card in the game.
clues.peak: The loudest minute of the whole night, and it is only 9:15.
clues.peck: The small kiss she gives him after taking every book he bid.
clues.paced: He walked the length of the kitchen twice before throwing one card.
clues.ape: To copy. He bids whatever she just bid and it has never once worked.

clues.bailed: He got up at ten-thirty down two hundred. They still bring it up.
clues.abide: Live with it. The call was made, the call stands, on to the next.
clues.idea: Bidding nil with the ace of spades still sitting in your hand.
clues.lied: About the count, once, in 2004, and it is still the first thing anybody says.
clues.bled: Points, three at a time, all night, with nobody noticing until the end.
clues.idle: Sitting this round out, watching, and not permitted to say one word.

clues.gasped: All four did it at once when the little joker fell on the first book.
clues.page: Torn off, folded in half, tucked under the sugar bowl for next Friday.
clues.sage: Whoever she is at your table: she says the rule out loud and it is over.
clues.gaps: The holes in his suits, which she counted two rounds ago.
clues.ages: How long the man on the left takes to bid. Every single time.
clues.pads: Yellow, legal, one per year, in a stack in the same drawer.

clues.arched: One eyebrow, and the bid across the table dropped by two.
clues.reach: He went for a card, hovered over it, and pulled his hand back.
clues.heard: Everything at this table is, including what you said under your breath.
clues.hard: The ten of spades on the first lead. That is a message, not a mistake.
clues.dare: Go on and cut it. She did not say it out loud and she did not have to.
clues.herd: To move a group along, which is what she does to four grown adults who cannot decide.

clues.graced: She sat down at eight and the whole table straightened up.
clues.grace: What she shows the man who set her last week, by dealing him in again.
clues.rage: Two seconds of it, then a laugh, then he shuffles.
clues.card: One of thirteen, and somehow always the wrong one.
clues.drag: The long stretch between the bid and the first lead while he sorts twice.
clues.dear: What she calls him right before she cuts his ace.

clues.praise: The team goes up ten minutes before the choir does, and the room is standing by the second song.
clues.raise: What the hands do without being told, all down the row, on the run into the chorus.
clues.pairs: White gloves come out of her purse in twos, one set for her and one for whoever forgot.
clues.spare: The extra offering envelope she keeps in her Bible for the visitor sitting beside her.
clues.rise: What the whole building does on the last verse, and the ushers step back off the doors.
clues.ears: The sound man's, and the exact second he pulls the guest preacher's mic back down.

clues.choirs: Three of them here: the mass, the youth, and the men's, and only one gets second Sunday.
clues.choir: The A selection is theirs. The B selection is why Thursday rehearsal ran until ten.
clues.rich: Not a word for this congregation. A word for what eleven voices do in a room built for sixty.
clues.sir: What the junior usher calls a man twice his age, because the board taught him to.
clues.his: Whose robe went missing before the anniversary, and who alone carries the closet key.
clues.chi: The Greek letter standing in for Christ in the shorthand painted on the fellowship hall banner.

clues.gloves: Cotton, white, and a fresh set in her vestibule drawer for the girl on the junior board.
clues.glove: One hand up, one hand folded, and the cotton on both means she is working, not visiting.
clues.solve: What the board does with a full room and four empty seats, in under a minute, without speaking.
clues.egos: What the minister of music and the drummer have been managing between them since March.
clues.lose: What she will not do: the count, the keys, or her place at the back of the sanctuary.
clues.ogle: What you do not do to a visitor's crown, no matter how wide the brim gets.

clues.rushed: Nothing about the eleven o'clock is, and the parking lot at one-thirty settles the argument.
clues.usher: She stands the whole hour at the door and seats you when the song allows, not when you arrive.
clues.herds: What the megachurch parking team does with two hundred cars and one working exit.
clues.hers: The chair by the vestibule window. It has a cushion on it and nobody has to be told.
clues.dues: What the auxiliary collects in January, in cash, into a ledger she takes home with her.
clues.sure: How the woman in the front row says a thing once, and it becomes the plan.

clues.maiden: The surname the mothers still use for her in the roll book, sixty years after the wedding.
clues.amend: What the clerk does to the minutes when the trustees remember the vote differently.
clues.aide: Armor-bearer is the word here: water, towel, and the Bible carried a half-step behind.
clues.mind: What she made up about the carpet color, and the trustee meeting is a formality.
clues.dime: What went into the plate from a child's hand, and the woman beside her did not correct it.
clues.named: Cut in brass beside the fellowship hall door, after the vote, and she was in the room for it.

clues.remain: What the mothers do after the benediction, seated, while the building empties around them.
clues.rein: What the board chair keeps on a young minister who wants to change the order of service.
clues.rain: Why the church van makes two trips, and why the ushers keep towels stacked by the door.
clues.near: Where the nurses' unit sits: aisle end, two rows back, in white, watching everything.
clues.earn: Nobody does the front pew. You are seated in it by somebody, or you are not.
clues.mine: What the sopranos call the alto line the week the director reassigns it.

clues.humane: What the benevolence fund is for: a light bill, a bus ticket, and no questions in the meeting.
clues.human: What the pastor admits to being, once, from the pulpit, and the room goes very quiet.
clues.ahem: The clerk's, into a live mic, when the reading has gone four minutes past its slot.
clues.mean: What she does not have to be. She simply looks, and the whole back row sits down.
clues.hum: What the keyboard holds under the altar call, low, until somebody finally comes down.
clues.menu: Typed for the repast and taped inside the hall door, and the family never sees a bill.

clues.easily: Nothing about a three-hour Women's Day program happens this way, and no one expected it to.
clues.aisle: Hers to run, and the child who bolts up it during prayer gets caught by the elbow.
clues.seal: What the clerk presses into the certificate before the baptism goes into the book.
clues.easy: How the drummer starts the shout music, and it is not, and the whole room knows better.
clues.yes: What the mothers' board says, and only then does the trustee board pretend it decided.
clues.lays: What the nurse in white does over the woman who caught the spirit, quick, without a word.

clues.fasten: What she does to the hat pin at the door, so the crown will not move for three hours.
clues.safe: Bolted into the pastor's office, and the two women with the combination are not the pastor.
clues.seat: There are seven in the front row and every one of them belongs to a woman by name.
clues.sent: The sick-and-shut-in card, in her hand, every Monday, with stamps she buys herself.
clues.nest: The choir loft after service: three hymnals, two hats, and somebody's reading glasses.
clues.east: Which way the old sanctuary was built to face, and why the sun hits the third pew at eleven.

clues.mouths: Forty of them open on the same word, and the third row can hear which one came in early.
clues.shout: The music behind it: two chords, the drummer, and not one person sitting down.
clues.south: Where the pastor's people came up from, which is why devotional service still opens the morning.
clues.must: What the basement smells like in August, and the trustees have been told about it twice.
clues.thou: The pronoun the old deacon still prays in, and nobody has ever asked him to stop.
clues.most: What the eleven o'clock has of everything: cars, children, and folks who came for one song.

clues.pianos: The upright in the annex and the one up front, and only one has been tuned this year.
clues.pains: What the eighty-two-year-old at the keyboard plays straight through, and she has not missed a Sunday.
clues.pins: In the hat, in the corsage, and in the little cushion she keeps in the vestibule drawer.
clues.naps: The child laid across two laps in the fourth pew, out cold before the offering is lifted.
clues.span: Sixty-one years between the oldest usher on duty and the youngest, and both are on the door.
clues.spin: What the young minister of music put on the anniversary hymn, and the mothers had thoughts.

clues.probes: What the finance committee does to the roof estimate: line by line, twice, before any vote.
clues.robes: Burgundy with gold, forty-two of them, and one woman holds the key to that closet.
clues.sober: How the second service runs at the campus church: lights low, no tambourine, out in seventy minutes.
clues.prose: What the announcements turn into, when they were only ever supposed to be a list.
clues.ropes: The stanchion kind across the last four pews, until the board opens them at the second song.
clues.reps: The three run-throughs of the anniversary selection, Thursday night, after everybody worked all day.

clues.bolder: What the youth choir got by the third verse, once the church mothers stood up behind them.
clues.lord: The word the whole room says back to her, uncued, the moment she opens the devotional.
clues.older: The two women walked in on an arm, and the service does not begin until they are down.
clues.role: Hers is nowhere on the printed program, and the building would stall by ten past eleven without it.
clues.lore: Which pew flooded in '96, which pastor left in '04. She has all of it and no one wrote it down.
clues.bored: The teenager in the balcony, right up until the drums come in on the second chorus.

clues.losing: What the roll book says about the fourth pew, and why she is on the phone Monday morning.
clues.lingo: Tarry service, A and B selection, armor-bearer. Nobody explains a word of it to a visitor.
clues.sing: What six hundred people do when the power cuts out: no keyboard, no mic, still on pitch.
clues.sign: Out front, plastic letters, and the title she changes Tuesday with a suction cup pole.
clues.oils: Anointing, in a little bottle in her purse, and she reaches the hospital before the pastor does.
clues.lions: Daniel's, drawn on butcher paper down the basement wall for children's church.

clues.broken: The third step up to the loft, since spring, and the trustees have priced the repair twice.
clues.broke: What the church was in 1994, and the eleven women who took up a Friday collection until it wasn't.
clues.bone: What the old song says the Lord can do with the dry ones, and the balcony stands for that verse.
clues.born: What the testimony always circles back to, and she gives the date and the street address.
clues.knob: Missing off the basement door since Easter, and everybody knows to push it with a hip.
clues.one: How many services a storefront keeps, and it holds forty people at capacity.

clues.bronze: The plaque by the door with the founding members on it, and two of them are still in the building.
clues.zone: What the ushers cut the sanctuary into, four of them, one woman answering for each.
clues.zero: Where the building fund started in January, and the thermometer on the wall is filled in by hand.
clues.bore: Not what ninety minutes of preaching is, if the man behind you is keeping time on the pew back.
clues.nor: The word in the old benediction, neither this ___ that, and half the room says it right along.
clues.bro: What the young men call each other out in the lot at one-thirty, out of their mothers' hearing.

clues.dragon: The red one out of Revelation, and the guest evangelist drew it on the easel pad in marker.
clues.grand: The march at the anniversary: two by two down the center, oldest board first, nobody hurrying.
clues.road: Eleven miles of it for the pastor who serves two charges, and the second service starts at three.
clues.rang: The office phone, all Monday, about one line in yesterday's announcements.
clues.nod: Hers, from the rear of the sanctuary, and only then do the doors come open.
clues.darn: What the seamstress does to a hem in the vestibule, ten minutes before the processional.

clues.lacked: What his hand did all night. He bid six anyway, and he made it, and nobody has recovered.
clues.deal: Her turn, and she squares the pile twice before a single card moves.
clues.deck: Fifty-two, minus the two jokers somebody's nephew lost in 2011.
clues.lack: What nobody at this table will admit to, least of all after a set.
clues.lead: The first card down, and the whole hand turns on whether she went low or high.
clues.ace: The one card he holds back too long, every time, and she counts on it.

clues.crowns: Two of them in the case: this year's and the one the chapter had made back in 1969.
clues.crown: Rhinestones on loan from the same shop since 1988, and it has never once fit anybody.
clues.owns: The alumnae chapter does, not the school, and they bring it in a locked case.
clues.worn: Her mother's pearls, out on loan for the night and back in the box by Sunday.
clues.rows: The front three are held for the alumnae chapter, and nobody tests that.
clues.won: What her platform did in the campus vote. Turnout, not the gown.

clues.floats: The parade has four, and two of them are a flatbed with crepe paper and a good speaker.
clues.float: Chicken wire, tissue paper, and three nights in the ag barn before Saturday.
clues.flats: She changes into them at the corner of Third, heels in her hand, still marching.
clues.last: The engineering club's entry rolls at the end every year, and it has never broken down.
clues.lost: The little cousin, for four whole minutes, between the fire truck and the pep squad.
clues.salt: What the town spread in 2019, when the parade route iced over in October.

clues.stride: Nine people hit the boards at once and the sound gets there before the movement does.
clues.rites: The parts of the show that never change, because the chapter of 1971 is watching.
clues.tried: Out for the line four times before they took her, and now she calls the cadence.
clues.tires: The bus rolled in on four bald ones from a chapter three states over.
clues.rest: Ninety seconds between sets, and not one person uses it to sit down.
clues.tier: The upper level fills first, because that is where you can actually see the formations.

clues.staged: The coronation looked effortless. Three rehearsals, a lighting cue sheet, and her clipboard.
clues.stage: Built Thursday in the gym, struck Sunday, and the risers go back to the music department.
clues.dates: Two schools, one weekend in October, and the alumni office locked them in a year out.
clues.gates: Open at ten. The line for the field house started forming somewhere around six.
clues.sage: The retired dean of students, eighty-four, who still gets the first word at the luncheon.
clues.seat: Section F, row 12. The same four people have held it since the Clinton administration.

clues.gather: Nobody organizes it. By nine Friday the parking lot behind the gym is simply full.
clues.heart: Where the weekend actually lives: forty folding chairs behind a church-school gym.
clues.great: The class of '74 says theirs was the last real one. The class of '89 says the same.
clues.hear: You can tell whose band it is from a mile off, and the small school's is thirty people.
clues.tear: In her eye when the roll of departed classmates is read at the Sunday service.
clues.rage: What the shuttle driver holds in for four hours of the same six blocks.

clues.loathe: What she does to the third-floor ice machine, and she books the same room anyway.
clues.hotel: Sold out since March. The overflow is forty minutes up the interstate in Meridian.
clues.late: Check-in is three. The lobby is a full reunion by noon and the desk gave up arguing.
clues.hate: What the front desk clerk, a junior on work-study, will not admit to by Saturday.
clues.oath: The one the new chapter officers take at the alumnae breakfast, hands flat on the table.
clues.tale: The one about the '81 bus breaking down, and it grows a new detail every October.

clues.clothe: What four generations of one family do for Saturday, in the same two colors.
clues.cloth: Vinyl, school colors, clipped to the folding table because the wind comes off the field.
clues.echo: The chant from the far end of the pavement comes back at you two seconds later.
clues.hole: In the '94 shirt, under the arm, and she wears it every single October regardless.
clues.lot: Gate C. Space assignments by chapter, and the map went out in September.
clues.toe: Her heel sank in the grass, so she is walking the rest of the route on the front of one foot.

clues.editor: Nineteen years on the alumni magazine, and she knows which photographs start fights.
clues.doer: The chapter president who actually shows up Thursday to unload the truck herself.
clues.redo: The cover, twice, because the first one cropped the small school's band right out.
clues.riot: The comment section under the parade photographs, and she moderates it personally.
clues.rode: Twelve hours from Houston in a van with four classmates and one good playlist.
clues.tore: The '68 banner, on the fence, and the archivist has already asked for the pieces.

clues.garnet: One of the two colors. The other is gold, and the exact shade is named in a 1911 charter.
clues.grant: The city gave one for the parade barricades, and the alumnae chapter matched it.
clues.anger: What the bookstore caused by ordering the sweatshirts in the wrong shade of red.
clues.gear: Two duffels: one for the field on Saturday, one for the black-tie thing that night.
clues.rent: The homecoming committee pays it on a storage unit twelve months of the year.
clues.near: The hotel is not. The house she grew up in is four blocks from the stadium.

clues.argyle: His sweater vest, on the first tee at seven a.m., unchanged since the Reagan years.
clues.early: Shotgun start at seven for the scholarship tournament, and the foursomes filled in June.
clues.large: The only size left on the table by Saturday, which is of course nobody's size.
clues.layer: Forty degrees at kickoff, eighty by the afternoon, and she dressed for both.
clues.relay: Alumni against students at halftime, and the fifty-year-olds keep winning the thing.
clues.year: The number under her name at the registration table, and it settles every argument.

clues.course: The one class she still talks about, and the professor who taught it is at the luncheon.
clues.source: Who the campus paper calls when they need the real numbers on the endowment.
clues.score: Nobody in the parking lot can tell you it at halftime, and nobody is bothered.
clues.sore: The knee that says no to a second flight of stadium steps, and she takes them anyway.
clues.ours: How the alumnae say the yard, forty years after they last had a key to anything.
clues.rouse: What a drumline does to a crowd that was asleep in lawn chairs ten seconds ago.

clues.courts: Both schools bring one, and the photographers make them stand together at midfield.
clues.court: Queen, king, and the attendants, elected in September by the whole student body.
clues.cost: The gown, the shoes, the photographer: eleven hundred, and her line sisters split it.
clues.tours: The admissions office runs them all weekend, for visiting kids and their mothers.
clues.cuts: The registrar made them to the Friday schedule so classes end at noon.
clues.rust: On the folding chairs that come out of the same storage unit every October.

clues.jesuit: Xavier in New Orleans. Fifteen hundred students, mass on Sunday, and a pharmacy school.
clues.suite: The one room the chapter books with a kitchenette, and everybody ends up in it.
clues.suit: Seersucker, and he has had it pressed for this specific Saturday since 1997.
clues.ties: Bow, clip-on, or borrowed from a roommate ten minutes before the brunch.
clues.just: How many the whole college enrolls: eight hundred, and the dean knows most of the names.
clues.site: The old campus, four buildings and a chapel, on the national register since 1974.

clues.agents: One per class year, and they call every name on the list before the giving deadline.
clues.agent: The class of '99's is a dentist in Charlotte who has never once missed her number.
clues.tens: What the little cousins get handed at the entrance, folded, with instructions.
clues.sang: The alma mater, all four verses, and the ones who know two of them hum the rest.
clues.ages: The spread under one canopy: eighty-nine down to a baby in a school-colors onesie.
clues.ants: Whatever you set on the grass finds them in a minute. Everything goes on the table.

clues.gasket: Blew one outside Tuscaloosa in '08, and the story has improved every October since.
clues.steak: On the grill at the dentist's canopy, while everybody else is eating wings from a foil pan.
clues.takes: The drive, if you leave before the Thursday traffic. Fourteen hours if you do not.
clues.task: Hers is the shuttle schedule and the wristbands, and it has been hers for nine years.
clues.tags: The hanger on the mirror, plus a license plate from four states over.
clues.gate: Where the shuttle drops you, and where you will lose your whole group for an hour.

clues.outage: The power at the tents died at nine Saturday and three chapters shared one generator.
clues.auto: The one she drove up from Mobile, with a decal in the back window from 1993.
clues.goat: The argument under the canopy: best quarterback the school ever had, settled by nobody.
clues.tug: What the wind does to the canopy legs somebody forgot to weight down.
clues.gut: The feeling in her stomach walking into the chapel for the first time in a decade.
clues.out: The lights, the coolers, and the last three people, at two in the morning.

clues.listen: What the old heads tell the freshmen to do at the alumni panel. Some of them do.
clues.silent: The auction at the scholarship brunch: forty items, one clipboard, and a war over a jersey.
clues.lines: Four at the registration table, sorted by decade, and the one for the '70s moves slowest.
clues.list: Taped inside the canopy: who brings the ice, who brings the chairs, who brings nothing.
clues.lens: The photographer's, a foot long, and she has shot this weekend for twenty-two years.
clues.lets: The dean hears the step practice at one in the morning and, this weekend only, allows it.

clues.theirs: Whose weekend it is depends who you ask: the students living it, or the class of '94.
clues.shirt: Class year across the back in three-inch numbers, and the dues paid for the whole order.
clues.heirs: The grandchildren at the tailgate, in school colors, before they can spell the school.
clues.hers: The canopy, the coolers, the folding tables. All of it, and everybody knows it.
clues.hires: The alumni office takes on three student workers for the weekend, and pays them on time.
clues.rise: The whole section stands when the 1975 queen is walked out at halftime.

clues.comers: First-timers. Somebody's coworker who has never once seen anything like this.
clues.comes: What the class of '84 does every October, recession or not, funeral or not.
clues.more: What the DJ plays at midnight when the pavement was supposed to clear at eleven.
clues.some: Of that class, a good number pledged nothing at all and have not missed a weekend since.
clues.rose: Laid on the memorial bench for the classmate who did not make it to this one.
clues.core: Eleven people who never left the state, and they hold the entire thing together.

clues.barely: What anybody under the canopy could tell you about the third quarter.
clues.able: Ninety-one, uses a walker on the grass, and still does the whole parade route.
clues.bear: To carry it: the flag, the banner, the name of a class that is down to nine people.
clues.real: What the rivalry is, and the two athletic directors are godparents to each other's kids.
clues.rely: What the committee does on the same eleven volunteers, year after year after year.
clues.bare: The field at seven Sunday morning, except for one canopy nobody has claimed.

clues.alight: What forty-two people do off the charter bus, in heels, at eleven at night.
clues.light: The first of the morning, and the tent stakes are already going into the ground.
clues.hail: What the alma mater does to the school by name, right there in the opening line.
clues.halt: What the parade does for nine minutes at Fifth while the band sets a formation.
clues.tail: The end of the whole procession: the fire truck, and then the street sweeper.
clues.hit: The one song that gets everybody up, and it is the same one it was in 1998.

clues.instep: The high arch of the foot; a well-made loafer creases right across it by year two.
clues.step: One count. Left, and the weight moves with you.
clues.spin: He turns her out and catches her hand coming back, right on the four.
clues.spent: Two hours on a Tuesday, and the only thing she has to show is a better walk.
clues.pins: Her hair is laid, the wrap held with two of these, and it will not move all night.
clues.tips: The toe ends of a pair, worn pale from a thousand pivots on hardwood.

clues.lowest: The count where you dip. Knees soft, chin up, and back before the next bar.
clues.towel: Folded over his shoulder by the third song, because the hall runs hot in August.
clues.welts: What the new patent leather leaves across the top of her foot by midnight.
clues.west: The side of Chicago that gets named first whenever the argument starts.
clues.slot: The gap in the second row that opens when somebody sits a song out early.
clues.twos: The count everybody learns before anything else: one and one, over and over.

clues.elbows: Kept in, never out. Swing them wide in a crowded line and you will hear about it.
clues.elbow: The bend in the arm that a good frame keeps absolutely quiet.
clues.below: Under the hem is where you look if you actually want to learn the footwork.
clues.sole: Suede, brushed with a wire brush, so it slides on a gym floor and grips on wood.
clues.bows: At the end of the set he inclines his head and she nods back. That is the ceremony.
clues.blew: The DJ's speaker gave out mid-song and the line kept going without it.

clues.halter: Ties at the neck, backless, and she picked it because her arms have work to do.
clues.alter: What the teacher does to a pattern when the room is too full to travel.
clues.later: The advanced hour starts when the beginners clear out, and it runs past midnight.
clues.heart: What the tradition runs on, and what her doctor says is in better shape than his.
clues.halt: One raised palm from the front of the room and forty people stop mid-count.
clues.real: The difference between a class routine and what happens at a set on Saturday.

clues.breath: What you run out of on the fourth song, which is how you know you stopped coming.
clues.bathe: First thing when he gets home at two in the morning, before anything goes in the closet.
clues.earth: Where her weight stays. Nothing bounces, nothing hops, the floor gets all of it.
clues.rate: Ninety-something beats a minute is the pocket. Faster than that is a different dance.
clues.tear: What the seam of his slacks did on the drop, and he finished the song anyway.
clues.hater: The one leaning on the wall saying it looks easy, who will not come out on the floor.

clues.others: The three rows behind the front, watching her feet and landing half a count late.
clues.shoe: One pair lives in the trunk of the car and touches no sidewalk, ever.
clues.short: The version taught to beginners: sixteen counts, no turn, no styling.
clues.rest: Between songs: the fanning, the water, and somebody's aunt saying just one more.
clues.host: Whoever rented the hall collects at the door and remembers every single face.
clues.those: The ones who learned it in the seventies and never needed a class in their lives.

clues.absent: The cousin who swore he was coming to class and has now missed four Tuesdays.
clues.beats: Eight of them make the pattern, and she counts them out loud for the back row.
clues.best: What the room agrees she is. Nobody argues, and she never says it herself.
clues.seat: Nobody is using one after nine o'clock; the whole room is up on its feet.
clues.neat: How the footwork looks when it is right. Small, tidy, nothing wasted.
clues.bent: Knees stay soft the whole song. Lock them and you will feel it tomorrow.

clues.cheats: Skipping the turn and just walking the eight counts. She sees it from across the room.
clues.teach: What she does Tuesday nights for twenty dollars, and has since her knees were younger.
clues.chase: The pattern where she travels and he follows her line clear across the floor.
clues.aches: Sunday morning, both hips, and worth every minute of it.
clues.chest: Held up, shoulders down. The posture that tells the room you have had a class.
clues.haste: Rushing the count is the beginner's tell. The music is not going anywhere.

clues.duties: Who books the hall, who makes the flyer, who brings the aux cord. All assigned. All women.
clues.duet: Two people, one frame, and if it looks like one body moving, it worked.
clues.suit: Pressed, cream colored, and he will not sit down in it before the second set.
clues.tied: Double-knotted at the start of the night so nothing comes loose on a turn.
clues.dust: What she shakes onto a sticky gym floor, from a bottle she has had for years.
clues.side: The travel goes this way, not forward, and that is what beginners keep getting wrong.

clues.listed: Every class on the flyer, Tuesday through Sunday, all of it in her handwriting.
clues.slide: The one everybody knows: four walls, a quarter turn, and the whole reception joins in.
clues.list: What she keeps of who has paid and who is still promising to.
clues.tiles: Waxed squares in the church basement, and you can hear the whole room on them.
clues.tide: How the line moves. One row forward, everybody at once, then back.
clues.lets: She never turns a beginner down. One song, and she counts it in his ear.

clues.misled: He learned it off a phone video and has been doing the turn backwards for a year.
clues.smile: What she gives him anyway when he finally lands on the right count.
clues.miles: Forty each way from the south suburbs, every Tuesday, for one hour of class.
clues.dimes: Turning on one is the whole point, and it takes about a year to get there.
clues.mild: How she corrects. Quiet, one word, and nobody else in the room hears it.
clues.slim: The margin between on the beat and just behind it, which the room can always see.

clues.posted: Taped to the door of the hall back in September and not changed since.
clues.posed: He stopped moving to be admired mid-song and lost the count entirely.
clues.spot: Eyes on one mark on the back wall so the turn does not take you down with it.
clues.stop: When the record ends, forty people freeze on the last count and the room laughs.
clues.opted: She chose the partner dance over the line dance and has not looked back.
clues.dote: How the old heads treat a teenager who shows up alone and actually tries.

clues.poster: Photocopied, taped in the beauty shop window: Steppers Set, Saturday, dress code enforced.
clues.sport: What the men call it when their wives ask why they are gone every Tuesday night.
clues.store: The one place downtown that still carries suede bottoms in his size.
clues.sore: Where the new pair rubbed, one heel, and she danced on it the rest of the night.
clues.rose: What the noise in the room did when the couple in their eighties took the floor.
clues.pros: The ones who compete, drive to Detroit for it, and did not come here to socialize.

clues.purest: The oldest form of it. No tricks, no dip, just the walk done perfectly.
clues.purse: Left under her chair with the keys in it, and nobody has ever once touched it.
clues.setup: Table at the door, speaker in the corner, floor swept, all of it done by seven.
clues.upset: What he was when the count got away from him in front of everybody.
clues.sure: She never looks down at her own feet, not once, the entire song.
clues.true: Beat-perfect, and the old heads will say so out loud, which they rarely do.

clues.motels: Two nights outside Detroit for the weekend set, four ladies to a room.
clues.motel: Where the out-of-town crowd changes in the parking lot before walking in.
clues.melts: What the room does when the DJ finally puts on something slow.
clues.stole: Draped over her shoulders on the way in, off before the first song ends.
clues.most: Of the forty people in that room, more than half are women, and it is not close.
clues.lots: Gravel outside the hall where folks sit in the car until they hear the good song.

clues.oldest: Eighty-one, still leading, and the floor clears a little when he walks out on it.
clues.told: What she does when a man rushes her. Says it once, plain, and he slows down.
clues.sold: Tickets for the anniversary set went in two days, every one of them through her.
clues.toes: Never landed on if the lead is doing his job properly.
clues.lose: What you do to the count the second you start watching your own feet.
clues.dole: How she hands out a compliment. One at a time, and you remember getting it.

clues.spring: What the good ones have in the knee, so the walk looks like it costs nothing.
clues.grip: Light. Two fingers and a palm. Anything harder and she will not dance with you twice.
clues.grins: Traded across the floor between two couples who have been rivals since 1994.
clues.rings: They come off before class, because they catch on fabric and on hands.
clues.sign: A small lift of her chin, and he knows the turn is coming.
clues.sing: The whole room does the second verse out loud and nobody drops the count.

clues.advise: What the old heads do from the edge of the floor, whether you asked them or not.
clues.aside: She pulls him off the floor for thirty seconds and fixes it in one sentence.
clues.divas: The two who arrive at eleven, fully dressed, and then dance every song after.
clues.saved: A song held back for her all night, and the man in the booth knows which one.
clues.avid: Three classes a week, two sets a month, and a notebook full of patterns.
clues.said: Spoken once at the door, and that settled the dress code argument for good.

clues.wealth: Not money. Sixty years of a dance handed down in one city and still taught for free.
clues.hale: Eighty-three, walks in without a cane, and stays until the lights come up.
clues.tale: How the hall got its name, retold by whoever is standing nearest the door.
clues.heat: Forty bodies, no air conditioning, and the windows painted shut since 1970.
clues.thaw: The first twenty minutes, when the room is stiff and nobody wants to go first.
clues.whet: What one good record does to a room that was ten minutes from going home.

clues.safety: Dark suits, earpieces, and the retired deputy who trains that ministry is somebody's grandmother.
clues.fast: Twenty-one days every January, no meat, and the daily scripture goes out on the church group text.
clues.yeast: None of it in the Communion bread, because that first meal was eaten by people in a hurry to leave.
clues.stay: What the deacons do at the altar rail after dismissal, until the last person kneeling gets up.
clues.aye: How the clerk records each trustee in the minutes when a motion carries, one name at a time.
clues.teas: The urn in the fellowship hall after second service, hot water and honey, singers pouring first.

clues.inmate: The jail ministry writes forty of them by name, and the van goes upstate the second Saturday.
clues.mint: Out of her purse, cellophane crackling, passed down the pew to the coughing child mid-sermon.
clues.meant: What the deacon swears he did not do, once the bulletin announcement came out sideways.
clues.time: Twenty minutes a man on visiting day, and the sisters split the list before they sign in.
clues.neat: The old deacon's shirt, pressed by his own hand since his wife passed, collar sharp by seven.
clues.team: The dozen who ride upstate in the van: two drivers, one cooler, a box of stamped envelopes.

clues.salute: What the Men's Day program calls the part where the founders are named and the room stands.
clues.least: The Matthew 25 line the pastor preaches every November, about who you did it unto.
clues.salt: The bag the trustees set by the front steps in January, so nobody goes down on the ice.
clues.sale: Rummage in the fellowship hall, Saturday eight to two, and the ledger goes home with the treasurer.
clues.slate: The officers read out at the annual meeting, typed since October by the nominating chair.
clues.tales: What the old deacons trade in the vestibule about the pastor before this one, half of it true.

clues.famine: Joseph stored grain against it, and the basement pantry runs the same way: shelf full before the need.
clues.fan: Cardboard, wooden handle, the funeral home's name on the back, working harder than the window unit.
clues.amen: The corner where the deacons sit, and the one word back from it that keeps a preacher moving.
clues.men: A dozen of them cook and serve the annual breakfast, badly and proudly, one Saturday in October.
clues.main: The water line under the lot let go in February, and the treasurer cut the check that same day.
clues.fine: How everybody answers the greeter at the door, whether it is true that morning or not.

clues.herald: In 1865 the word still meant a man on a balcony with somebody else's paper in his hand.
clues.heard: Galveston, June nineteenth, and Texas finally got the news it had been kept from.
clues.read: What the committee does with the minutes book before one dollar gets voted on.
clues.held: The pageant is not on the courthouse lawn. That was never allowed. It is on ground they bought.
clues.hard: What thirty months of being kept in the dark was, and no part of the day pretends otherwise.
clues.lead: What the girls' drill team does, whistle and all, in front of the flatbed carrying the queen.

clues.shared: What the news was not, for two full cotton seasons. That is the whole reason for the date.
clues.share: What the program asks the oldest woman present to do, and she takes all the time she wants.
clues.shade: Under the pecans by ten, because the program runs long and it is June in Texas.
clues.hears: What the whole street does when the band turns the corner two blocks off.
clues.reads: How the order goes: the plainest language the government ever managed, and only five sentences.
clues.herd: What the trail riders bring into town ahead of the parade, and the avenue smells like it after.

clues.thread: The year stitched into the quilt corner by a woman who had no other way to write it down.
clues.earth: Ten acres of it in Houston, bought in 1872 by four men who had been born owned.
clues.heart: The reading is that. Everything else on the printed order is arranged around it.
clues.trade: What the county archive still records in dollars, with a first name and no surname after it.
clues.date: June nineteenth, not the first of January. Texas counts from when the word actually landed.
clues.tread: What the brick streets of Freedmen's Town were laid for, by hand, by the people living on them.

clues.parked: Ten acres in Houston, 1872, bought by freedmen because every other green space was closed to them.
clues.park: What Houston took title to in 1916, and what the neighborhood never once stopped calling its own.
clues.dark: When the pit crew lights it Thursday, so the beef is right by Saturday morning.
clues.peak: Noon, when the program reaches the order and even the children under the tent go quiet.
clues.dare: What it took to hold the second one in 1866, in a state that had just lost and was not sorry.
clues.reap: What the order never mentioned: land, or how a freed man was supposed to come by any.

clues.hearty: How the plate gets built at the grounds: nothing on it is small and the line moves slow.
clues.year: Eighteen sixty-three, sixty-four, sixty-five — all of them after the paper was already signed.
clues.heat: Eleven in the morning on the Gulf coast, and the program does not move indoors for it.
clues.teary: How the ninety-year-old gets at the second verse, which half the room has to hum.
clues.rate: What the judges score first: the recitation. Poise second. The dress not at all.
clues.yeah: What comes back from the crowd at the line about all slaves being free. Not applause. Just that.

clues.framed: The order, printed and hung in the hallway between the church anniversary photo and the diplomas.
clues.fade: What the mimeographed programs from the seventies did in her box, and she keeps every one.
clues.farm: What people walked off of upriver the week the word came down, and kept on walking.
clues.fear: The reason some waited for the crop to come in, and the reason others did not wait at all.
clues.red: Hibiscus once, strawberry soda now, and the color was never the point of it.
clues.made: What a surname was in 1865: chosen, written down, and defended ever since.

clues.charts: Pinned up in the church annex: which families came off which places, and where they went after.
clues.cash: What the scholarship is not. It is a check, and the bank teller already knows her name.
clues.star: The Texas one, bursting on the flag Ben Haith drew in 1997, over an arc for the new horizon.
clues.arts: The recitation contest: General Order No. 3 from memory, and the eleven-year-old misses nothing.
clues.cart: What the ice came in on, in blocks, before anybody at the grounds had a machine.
clues.hats: White and wide, on the ushers who walk the elders to their seats, and nobody argues with them.

clues.traced: What she did through the county deed books until she found the name and the year they bought.
clues.cedar: The chest the church minutes live in, 1867 forward, and she keeps the only key to it.
clues.care: What the roadside marker gets twice a year, from one woman, with a wire brush.
clues.acre: Freedom colonies: bought cheap, worked hard, and a few of those towns are still on the map.
clues.race: What they run at the fairgrounds before the bull riding, and the announcer knows everybody's people.
clues.card: Handed out at the door: order of service on one side, the words to the anthem on the other.

clues.grated: Nutmeg over the ice cream the church ladies crank by hand on the side lawn.
clues.great: Her grandmother's grandmother stood on the Strand in 1865. That is four names, and she can say all four.
clues.gate: The one at the county fairgrounds that stayed shut to them, which is why the rodeo has its own.
clues.age: What the oldest man present is asked, into the microphone, and he takes his time answering.
clues.grade: What Texas schools let out for long before any calendar up north carried the day at all.
clues.gear: Saddle, rope and a good hat, loaded Friday night for the ride into town.

clues.flared: What the pageant skirts do on the turn, sewn across three living rooms over five weeks.
clues.fled: What some did that same afternoon, on foot, toward a county where they had people waiting.
clues.deal: What the order offered in place of land: wages, and a strong suggestion to stay where they were.
clues.fare: Two dollars round trip on the chartered bus down to the island, and the church covers the children.
clues.leaf: The shade at the far end where the domino table sets up and does not move until dusk.
clues.real: Absolute equality of personal rights: five words in the order, argued into being one century at a time.

clues.fedora: Grey, brushed the night before, and it does not leave his head once, not even at the pit.
clues.road: The one out of the port in June 1865, full of people going to see about their own.
clues.era: What ended at Ashton Villa, and what began the next morning, which was the harder part.
clues.rode: How the queen goes down the avenue: on the back of a convertible somebody waxed at dawn.
clues.redo: What the committee does to the program every spring, and the order of service never changes.
clues.fed: What it became in 2021, and half the offices that closed had never said the word out loud before.

clues.soared: What the second verse does once the older voices find it and the room stops pretending.
clues.soda: Big Red, by the case, and in this state that is not a trend or a joke. It is just what gets bought.
clues.rose: What the whole tent does when the flag with the bursting star comes up the aisle.
clues.dears: What the elders call the children they are correcting, right up until they mean it differently.
clues.sore: What the feet are by four, and why the pageant shoes come off on the church steps.
clues.ode: What the eighth grader's poem is, whether or not she would ever call it that.

clues.dreams: What the girl in the recitation says her great-grandmother was not permitted to have out loud.
clues.seam: Let out twice on the white dress, because she has grown since Easter and the pageant is in June.
clues.arms: What two thousand Union soldiers carried into Galveston, and the reason the paper got obeyed.
clues.sear: What the beef gets over pecan wood on Thursday night, before the long slow part begins.
clues.dear: What a printed name is, when it is the only one your family ever got to choose.
clues.same: The route the parade has taken longer than anybody living can remember: down the avenue, past the church.

clues.dreamt: The night of the eighteenth, 1865, when nobody on the island yet knew what the morning held.
clues.meat: Beef here, and links. Whatever they do with pork elsewhere is elsewhere's business.
clues.team: Eleven men cooking in shifts from Thursday dark to Saturday noon, off a schedule taped to the wall.
clues.read: What the man at the podium does slowly while everyone stands: no commentary, start to finish.
clues.term: Employer and hired labor: the words the order swapped in, and the world did not follow.
clues.tame: What the day is not, by four, when the band comes back out and the street fills up again.

clues.beards: White, on the four men in the front pew who were boys when their grandfathers still told it.
clues.bread: Baked Friday at the church so the Saturday kitchen only has to warm the pans.
clues.beads: Sewn onto the crown by hand, and it goes on the new one at the end of the night.
clues.based: Galveston. Not Washington, not Richmond. That is the argument every June with somebody from out of state.
clues.bears: What the marker on the seawall says in eighty words, and it took twenty years to get it put up.
clues.bared: What the order did in five sentences, about a thing every person in the room already knew.

clues.harden: What the seventy years after 1865 did to the promise, and the day still gets kept on time.
clues.earn: What the order said the freed would now do for wages, on the same ground, for the same man.
clues.hand: What the program was first set down by, in 1954, and the committee still uses her wording.
clues.near: Sixty miles between the port and places nobody told, and the road was open the whole time.
clues.head: Where the elders sit, and nobody takes those seats without being walked to them first.
clues.ran: What some could not do, because there was nowhere to go, and staying was its own decision.

clues.admire: What you cannot help doing at the ninety-four-year-old who has not missed a nineteenth since 1948.
clues.media: The trucks that turn up in 2021 and ask an elder to explain her whole life in thirty seconds.
clues.ride: What the queen's little brother gets on the fire truck, once, and talks about all year.
clues.idea: Whose it was to walk from Fort Worth toward Washington at eighty-nine, and keep walking until it passed.
clues.dime: What the children brought for the park fund, and the treasurer counted it in front of them.
clues.aimed: Where the committee's money goes: the scholarship first, the sound system second, the tent last.

clues.dearly: How the day is held by the people who kept it when no calendar anywhere else would.
clues.delay: Thirty months of it, with the paper already law the whole time. That is what the date is about.
clues.early: Four in the morning at the grounds, and the men at the pit have been there six hours.
clues.ready: What the contestant is, and has been since March, and she will tell you so herself.
clues.relay: How the word actually traveled in 1865: port to the next place, and the next, by mouth.
clues.yard: Of white cotton, bought for the ushers' sashes and cut out on her dining table.

clues.braved: What the people who put on the first ones did, before any law in Texas said they could gather.
clues.bear: What the descendants do with the name: carry it, and say it in full when anybody asks.
clues.rev: The bikes at the back of the line, kept idling until the drum majors clear the corner.
clues.drab: What the day is not. Every color is out, and the flag has its own.
clues.bad: What the roads inland were that June, and people walked them anyway to carry the news.
clues.ave: Emancipation, in Houston: the street the parade uses, and the name the neighborhood fought to restore.

clues.derail: What nobody ever managed to do to the observance, not in 1866, not in 1900, not in the quiet years.
clues.dial: What the chairwoman still does, from a paper list, to ninety households every May.
clues.lied: What the planters told the people through two cotton seasons, until one of them finally slipped.
clues.rail: The one the elders lean on going up the church steps, painted every spring before the nineteenth.
