clues.aide: The teenager assigned to the ninety-year-old for the whole program, with a fan and a cold bottle.
clues.lard: In the teacake dough, the way the recipe card says, and the card is in her mother's hand.

clues.chapel: Tuesday morning, required, and the registrar counts heads from the back row.
clues.place: Third row left. Nobody assigned it, and by October it is yours.
clues.heal: What the choir director says the ten quiet minutes before class are for.
clues.plea: The letter you write the dean of students. One page, no excuses.
clues.each: One by one, the way the president learns names at a school of nine hundred.
clues.ache: What the folding seats leave in your back by the benediction.

clues.denial: The letter from financial aid in March, and the appeal you file by Friday.
clues.nailed: Her thesis defense. The committee had no follow-up questions.
clues.dean: She knows your mother's maiden name and your registration hold, both.
clues.ideal: The four-year plan on the advising sheet, before the class got cancelled.
clues.idea: What the professor makes you defend out loud before she grants it.
clues.lend: The graphing calculator that moved through four rooms in one night.

clues.danger: The 1 a.m. alert text everybody screenshots and nobody quite believes.
clues.garden: The plot behind the ag building she has kept going since 1998.
clues.grade: Posted by ID number on the office door, and you count down the list.
clues.range: How far the tuba carries across the practice field at seven.
clues.nerd: The one who reset the printer for the whole floor and got no thanks.
clues.read: Forty pages before Thursday, and she opens with a pop quiz.

clues.pasted: Four layers of flyers on the same pole, and the top one is from October.
clues.taped: The lecture she recorded on her phone because the woman talks fast.
clues.past: Everything before you got here, which the mural in the union insists on.
clues.step: Yard show footwork, learned in a basement at 2 a.m. with the lights low.
clues.seat: Saved with a backpack in the caf, and defended.
clues.date: The registrar set it, and nobody's excuse moves it.

clues.stance: How she holds herself at the front of the line, still, before the first move.
clues.scent: Shea butter and press oil in the elevator of the women's dorm.
clues.cane: Painted, wrapped, and never set down where somebody could touch it.
clues.cast: The whole department showed for the fall play, professors in row two.
clues.neat: How the ironing board in the hall stays busy the night before an interview.
clues.cent: Counted twice at the campus store when the meal plan runs out.

clues.binder: Three rings, tabbed by week, and she has not lost a page since freshman year.
clues.diner: The place off campus open at 3, where the argument finally finishes.
clues.bird: The mascot suit, and only two people on this whole campus know who is in it.
clues.bred: Third generation here, and the building still remembers her grandmother.
clues.ride: Text the group chat Thursday, split the gas, four hours home.
clues.red: The ink she uses, and there is always more of it than you hoped.

clues.bridge: The walkway between the science hall and the library, crossed at 2 a.m.
clues.ridge: The long climb up from the first-year dorms. Nobody warns you about it.
clues.grid: The practice field chalked out, and the flag corps counting yardage.
clues.bide: What you do in the aid office line with a full battery and low hopes.
clues.dig: What the archives assistant lets you do in the basement boxes.
clues.rib: The gentle kind, from the professor who taught your mother.

clues.housed: Assigned by lottery in April, and the email lands at midnight.
clues.house: Not a building. The six of you on the third floor who cook together.
clues.shoe: Wiped at the door before the yard photo, every single time.
clues.dues: The chapter treasurer takes them by app now, and she posts who is behind.
clues.used: The ninety-dollar edition, four names already written inside the cover.
clues.shed: Where facilities keeps the folding chairs for every event on the yard.

clues.sundae: Soft serve at the end of the caf line, built in a paper cup.
clues.sedan: Parked crooked outside the library, hazards on, engine still running.
clues.sane: What the walk around the track at midnight is actually for.
clues.send: What the professor says about your draft at 11:58 p.m.
clues.sand: The court behind the rec, where intramurals go when the gym is booked.
clues.sun: Already hot at eight, and the class is all the way across campus.

clues.amends: What you make with your roommate before the housing form is due.
clues.named: The building carries her, and the plaque explains why in four sentences.
clues.mean: What the average has to be for the scholarship to renew in the fall.
clues.mend: What the tailor two blocks off campus does for eight dollars.
clues.made: The dean's list, and the way your grandmother says it on the phone.
clues.send: What the registrar will not do with your transcript until the balance clears.

clues.agency: Whose office you call about the grant, and she picks up on the second ring.
clues.cagey: How the roommate gets when you ask her who she was with.
clues.cage: The batting one behind the field house, free with a school ID.
clues.acne: What the health center hands you something for, without a lecture.
clues.age: Twenty-six in a first-year seminar, and the only one doing the reading.
clues.yen: The pull toward home around week nine, when nothing has gone wrong exactly.

clues.canter: The riding program at the land-grant school, and the 6 a.m. barn shift.
clues.cater: What the alumnae chapter pays somebody to do for the scholarship luncheon.
clues.crate: Milk one, flipped over, holding up the speaker out on the yard.
clues.rent: Due the first, and the off-campus apartment does not wait on your refund.
clues.ante: What the study group raises the week finals start.
clues.tear: The gown at the fitting, and the seamstress fixes it in ten minutes.

clues.ardent: How she talks about this school to anybody who will sit still for it.
clues.trade: Two shifts at the caf swapped over text, no manager involved.
clues.tread: Worn off the marble stairs by a hundred years of the same climb.
clues.trend: What the yard picks up on Monday and is finished with by Friday.
clues.dent: In the door of the car she drove all four years and still has.
clues.rate: What the credit union on the corner offers, in writing, no table required.

clues.advent: The wreath up front, one candle a week, and the choir rehearsing at seven.
clues.vent: What the third-floor lounge is for the night grades post.
clues.tend: What the campus minister does, quietly, for the ones who stopped calling home.
clues.van: Fifteen seats, the choir tour, and the sign-out sheet in her office.
clues.tea: Poured in real cups when the honors society inducts, and you dress for it.
clues.den: The lounge with the TV nobody controls and the couch everybody claims.

clues.byline: Your name in ten-point type over four hundred words on the parking policy.
clues.line: Out the door of the business office on the first of the month.
clues.bye: The week the schedule gives back, and the coach calls practice anyway.
clues.lie: What the attendance policy is, right up until the morning she checks.
clues.nil: The balance you are chasing, and the only number that clears the hold.
clues.bin: Blue, by the mailroom, where the extra copies of the paper end up.

clues.rained: Every year on outdoor convocation, and the tent goes up at six anyway.
clues.drain: What the walk from the far lot in August does to a fresh press.
clues.rain: Nobody moves. The drumline finishes the cadence in it.
clues.near: The dorm two minutes from your eight o'clock, which you did not get.
clues.arid: August in Texas, and the window unit in the old hall is losing.
clues.rein: What the adviser hands over once she trusts you with the budget.

clues.dancer: Modern technique at eight, and she is the only one already warm.
clues.dance: Not the party. The class, barefoot, in the old gym with the good floor.
clues.cedar: The chest at the foot of the bed, sent from home with everything folded.
clues.care: What the housekeeper on your floor takes of forty people, by name.
clues.acre: The whole campus, and you can cross it in nine minutes flat.
clues.earn: Twelve hours a week in the library, applied straight to the bill.

clues.number: Three on the sides, one on top. Say it wrong and you live with it six weeks.
clues.numb: How your scalp feels the first cold minute under the guard.
clues.burn: What the clipper gets after the fourth head, and why he switches to the other set.
clues.menu: Taped by the mirror: fade 25, beard 10, kids under ten 15.
clues.men: Six grown ones waiting, and not one has glanced at the television since noon.
clues.run: What she does with the place: her name on the license, her rules on the wall.

clues.argued: Two hours on Jordan or LeBron, and nobody in it wanted to win, just to keep going.
clues.guard: Number two on the clippers, and the reason your mother said bring the picture.
clues.grade: What the middle-school report card said, read aloud by the man holding scissors.
clues.urge: The itch at week five that walks you in on a Tuesday with nothing scheduled.
clues.dare: Somebody bet the young barber he could not do a design freehand. He is sketching.
clues.rage: The one topic, his ex-wife's lawyer, that turns his voice all the way up.

clues.hairdo: What Mama called it, and she was not asking your opinion on the length.
clues.radio: The oldies station out of the back speaker, louder than the TV nobody watches.
clues.hard: How he presses at the nape, and you can feel every year he has been doing it.
clues.raid: What the middle school lets out and does to the waiting bench at 3:15.
clues.road: Forty minutes each way because you will not let anybody else near your head.
clues.aid: The styptic pencil and a torn strip of tissue, for the cut nobody will admit to.

clues.nickel: Five cents in the tip jar as a joke, and he keeps it taped to the mirror.
clues.neck: The part you cannot see, checked in the hand mirror while you nod like you can.
clues.line: Straight across the forehead, and if it is off by a hair the whole cut is off.
clues.lick: The one piece at the crown that stands up no matter what she puts on it.
clues.like: What you say when he spins you around, whether or not you do.
clues.clink: Coins into the jar by the door, which is how the whole room knows you tipped.

clues.pencil: White, sharpened flat, used to mark the edge before the razor commits.
clues.clip: What he does around the ears while telling you to put your chin down.
clues.pile: Under the chair by four o'clock: everybody's Saturday, swept into one.
clues.pin: Holds forty years of Polaroids to the corkboard by the door.
clues.nice: What the mother says when she means it is finally short enough.
clues.pen: Chained to the counter, for the check nobody under thirty writes anymore.

clues.client: Same head, same chair, every other Thursday since 2003.
clues.cent: He has not raised the price one of these since the shop moved across the street.
clues.lint: The brush and the powder, then the flick at your shoulder before you stand.
clues.tile: Black and white squares on the floor, cracked by the door, mopped anyway.
clues.tin: The old coffee can where the combs soak blue all day.
clues.tie: What the deacon loosens before he sits, and knots again at the mirror.

clues.permit: Framed crooked over the mirror, her name on it, renewed every two years.
clues.trim: Not a cut. Just take the weight off and leave the length alone.
clues.prime: Saturday morning, ten to two, the hours nobody here gives up.
clues.timer: Nobody sets one, but everybody knows a good fade takes forty minutes.
clues.term: The old word for the cut, still used here, whatever the kid in chair four says.
clues.time: Two hours on a Saturday, and you knew that when you walked in.

clues.import: The weight a haircut carries the week before a funeral.
clues.prom: Third Saturday in May, six kids deep, all wanting the same edge.
clues.trio: The three chairs still working, out of the five bolted to the floor.
clues.tip: Folded into his palm at the handshake, never left on the counter.
clues.pro: Twenty years on the same head. He does not measure anymore.
clues.top: Where the length stays when the sides go down to nothing.

clues.champs: Whoever is on the muted screen, and whoever is still defending the 1996 team.
clues.champ: What he calls the six-year-old to get him to sit still.
clues.camp: Where the boy is headed Sunday, which is why he is getting it low today.
clues.sham: What the old head calls the twenty-dollar designer fade down the block.
clues.amp: The little one behind the counter feeding the speaker through a taped cord.
clues.cap: What the boy puts back on the second he steps outside, ruining it.

clues.blades: Oiled, tapped clean, laid out in a row, and nobody else touches them.
clues.bald: The spot he never mentions and always cuts around.
clues.deal: Two heads for thirty on a slow Tuesday, and do not tell the whole block.
clues.sale: The clippers he got half off at the supply store and swears are better.
clues.lads: Three of them on the bench, phones out, waiting on the same barber.
clues.lead: Who is next. She keeps it in her head and she has never once been wrong.

clues.conked: How the old heads wore it before the fade, lye and all, and it burned.
clues.code: Nobody wrote it down: you do not take a man's regular slot, ever.
clues.coke: Glass bottle from the machine in the corner, still cold, still a dollar.
clues.done: He spins the chair, holds up the mirror, and that is the whole announcement.
clues.once: How many times he asks how you want it. Answer carefully.
clues.den: What the back room becomes after six, with the space heater and the good chairs.

clues.combat: What the Friday argument sounds like from the sidewalk and never actually is.
clues.comb: Snapped in half about once a month, and there is a new one in the blue jar.
clues.coat: Hung on the hook, because the cape goes over everything else.
clues.cat: The shop one, asleep in the window since before anybody here started working.
clues.mat: The rubber one he stands on all day, worn thin where he pivots.
clues.tab: What she lets the man from the corner store keep until the first.

clues.chains: Gold, doubled, lifted out of the way before the cape snaps shut.
clues.chin: Down. He says it once and taps it, and after that you just know.
clues.inch: How much his wife said to take. He takes half and calls it even.
clues.scan: What you do to the room from the door: who is here, whose turn, how long.
clues.shin: The part of your leg the footrest hits when the chair is pumped too high.
clues.can: Sprayed cold on the back of your neck at the end, asked for or not.

clues.bishop: He comes in Saturday at four so the collar sits right Sunday morning.
clues.shop: Two chairs, a window sign, and forty years on the same corner.
clues.ship: How the boxes of clipper oil arrive, and always about a week late.
clues.hip: The old barber's replacement, which is why he works off a stool now.
clues.hop: Two doors down for a sandwich while he finishes the head ahead of you.
clues.hips: What the young barber leans into all day, and what he will pay for at fifty.

clues.fabled: The cut everybody in here claims he invented, and only one of them did.
clues.fade: Skin at the bottom, full at the top, and the whole art is the part between.
clues.deaf: The old head in the corner is nearly it, which is why he talks the loudest.
clues.fled: What the four-year-old did when the clippers came on. Under the sink.
clues.able: She can cut anybody's head in here better, and every one of them knows it.
clues.fad: Every few years a new one walks in on somebody's phone screen.

clues.citrus: Half a lemon, rubbed on the board after fish and again on her own hands.
clues.crust: Rolled out with a jelly glass because the pin went missing sometime in 1994.
clues.cuts: She knows six by name at the meat counter and asks for the one not in the case.
clues.rust: What the iron gets if you leave it wet, and why she dries it over the flame.
clues.curt: How she answers when a guest asks whether that stove really runs hot. Five words.
clues.suit: What the tall pot does for greens and for absolutely nothing else in this house.

clues.merits: Her pound cake has them. You may say so once, then she hands you a plate.
clues.timers: The stove has two. She has not touched either one since the Ford administration.
clues.items: Four of them on the back of an envelope, in her hand, and she will not read it out.
clues.term: What she calls a sauce that broke, and it is not a word she uses in company.
clues.mist: What the window over the sink does the minute the greens hit the water.
clues.rest: What the meat does on the board for ten minutes while you keep your hands off.

clues.stupor: The state of the whole house at two o'clock, once the pot has been emptied.
clues.soup: Bones in a freezer bag since Thursday, and today they are the entire point.
clues.pour: Never from the bottle. Into her palm first, then in, and she calls that measuring.
clues.spurt: How the drippings jar comes alive the second a wet spoon goes into it.
clues.pots: Six of them, each with exactly one job. The tall one is only ever for greens.
clues.sour: The look she gives a man who reaches past her for the knife she keeps sharp.

clues.almost: How full she takes the pot. Any higher than that and you wear it to the sink.
clues.salt: By hand, out of a bowl, and there has not been a measuring spoon here in years.
clues.most: The share of the whole day's work that is finished before anybody else is up.
clues.slam: That drawer has never closed on its own. You give it a hip and it answers.
clues.mats: Cut from an old towel, under the hot pan, because the table was her mother's.
clues.oats: In the meatloaf, not breadcrumbs, and nobody has ever talked her out of it.

clues.forked: Straight down into the cake. Clean and it comes out; otherwise it goes back in.
clues.fork: The bent one in the drawer that she uses for everything and will not let you toss.
clues.fed: What she did for the whole block for thirty years without calling it work once.
clues.rode: The cake came up here in the floorboard of the car, boxed and wrapped in a towel.
clues.redo: What she makes you do to a broken sauce, from the start, while she stands there.
clues.doer: Not a talker. She is in the room at five with the apron already tied behind her.

clues.bakery: She was offered a storefront twice and said no twice. This kitchen is enough.
clues.baker: The title beside her name on the program, and she corrects anybody who says cook.
clues.bake: What she will not do in August, no matter who is asking or what it is for.
clues.year: How long the fruitcake sits wrapped in the pantry before it is fit to cut.
clues.key: The pantry has one. It lives on her ring and there has never been a second.
clues.rye: The dark loaf nobody else here likes, so she makes it small and eats it all week.

clues.backed: Two women, one recipe, and she stood by hers when the church put it to a vote.
clues.baked: Since four in the morning, and the whole house knew it before anybody got up.
clues.cake: Three layers, no box, and the method is not written down anywhere on this earth.
clues.deck: The cards get cleared off the table the minute the flour comes out. Every time.
clues.back: Where the good pan lives: far shelf, behind everything, out of reach on purpose.
clues.ace: What she is with a paring blade, and she is not handing it to you to find out.

clues.foiled: Every plate that leaves this house is covered and pressed down around the edges.
clues.foil: Two layers over the pan, tight, and you do not lift it in the car on the way.
clues.fold: Not stir. Under and over, twelve passes, and she counts them out loud for you.
clues.file: Three strokes on the steel before she cuts anything, standing right at the sink.
clues.life: How long that pan has been in this family: hers, her mother's, and one before.
clues.lid: It has not matched its pot since 1988. It still sits down flush and that is that.

clues.coiled: The burner, orange in a dark kitchen, and she reads it without touching the dial.
clues.coil: Wrapped and clipped, the cord on a mixer she bought in 1979 that still runs.
clues.cold: How the plate has to be before the icing goes anywhere near it. She will wait.
clues.code: The unwritten one: her pans, her drawer, her stove, and you ask before you touch.
clues.dice: Even squares off the flat of the blade, done before you have found a bowl.
clues.ice: The tray she still cracks by hand, because the machine kind tastes like the freezer.

clues.cloven: Split clean down the middle, the way the hoof is on what is in her deep freeze.
clues.oven: Runs fifty degrees hot. Everybody knows by exactly how much and nobody has called.
clues.once: How many times she tells you. There is no second telling in this room.
clues.novel: The paperback face-down on the counter while the pot gets on with its own business.
clues.lone: One stool pulled up to the counter at six in the morning, and it is hers.
clues.cone: Rolled out of wax paper on the spot when the piping bag cannot be found.

clues.blower: The fan in the hood, loud as a truck, and she runs it before anything hits the pan.
clues.bowl: The yellow one with the chip out of the rim. Sixty years of batter have been in it.
clues.blow: What she tells you not to do on it. Wait, or you taste nothing else all day.
clues.brew: The coffee goes on before the light does, and the first cup is not yours.
clues.lower: She will not take that flame down for anybody standing there looking impatient.
clues.elbow: Hers, out sideways, is how you learn you have stepped too close to the range.

clues.fruits: Peaches left on the sill until they give under a thumb, and not one hour sooner.
clues.sift: Twice, always, even though the bag swears up and down it has been done already.
clues.first: The pan on the front eye is hers, and it goes on before anything else does.
clues.fits: How the apron does after forty years. The ties go around her twice now.
clues.fist: The dough gets one, straight down, and then it gets left alone for a whole hour.
clues.stir: Constantly, one direction, and you do not walk away from that pot to answer a phone.

clues.detach: The head comes off the good mixer, and she is the only one who takes it apart.
clues.teach: She will not do it by measurement. Stand there and watch, or do not learn it.
clues.heat: Medium means her medium, which is about half of what you would have called it.
clues.date: On masking tape on every container in the freezer, in marker, without exception.
clues.ache: What her hands do in the cold, and she still cracks the eggs one at a time, one-handed.
clues.chat: The phone on her shoulder a full hour while her hands never once stop moving.

clues.bathed: The greens, three separate times, until the water in the sink finally runs clear.
clues.bathe: What the roast does in its own drippings every twenty minutes, door barely open.
clues.bath: The double boiler, which here is a bowl set over water, because she never bought one.
clues.beat: Three hundred strokes by hand. She counts them and she has never once been wrong.
clues.head: Of the garlic, smashed flat under the pan and peeled out in a single motion.
clues.tab: She keeps one on who has her dishes. A notebook, with names, and with dates.

clues.mobile: The little cart she rolls out, because there is no room to sit down in here.
clues.lime: Rolled hard under her palm on the counter first. That is where the juice comes from.
clues.mile: How far down the hall the smell gets before the first person knocks on the door.
clues.limb: The pecan tree out back, and the reason there is a bag of them in the freezer.
clues.oil: A film wiped onto the iron with a paper towel while the pan is still warm.
clues.limbo: Where the last slice sits: nobody will claim it and nobody will throw it out.

clues.adults: Only they carry the pot from the stove to the sink. That rule has never moved.
clues.adult: What you become here the day she hands you the knife and walks out of the room.
clues.dust: Flour over everything by seven, including the radio and the top of the icebox.
clues.stud: She found it herself and drove the nail in to hang the heavy pot. It has held.
clues.dual: Two ovens was the one thing she asked for, and the only remodel she ever wanted.
clues.lad: The grandson who wants to learn. He gets onions and nothing sharper than that yet.

clues.second: The one she puts on your plate while you are still saying no to it.
clues.once: You said no. That was the whole of your objection, and it did not survive.
clues.done: She decides when the meal is. Pushing your chair back early decides nothing.
clues.send: What she does with the leftover pans at the door, and refusing is not an option.
clues.den: Where the men drift at halftime while the table is still being cleared.
clues.nod: How permission to start eating gets given, and everybody is watching for it.

clues.breast: Two on the platter, and everybody knows which grandchild has a claim on one.
clues.best: The dishes that live behind glass all week and come out for this one meal.
clues.rest: What she takes only after the last plate is dried and the last pan put up.
clues.seat: The one at the head is not yours, and nobody has ever had to say so twice.
clues.stare: Sent across the table with no words attached, and the subject changes.
clues.bare: The table never is. Something goes down over the wood first, even for family.

clues.faster: How the children eat, hoping to get excused before the grown talk starts.
clues.feast: It is not one. It is a weekday menu on a Sunday schedule, every single week.
clues.after: The hours nobody schedules anything in, because you will still be at that table.
clues.safe: Where the silver sits Monday through Saturday, and she knows the combination.
clues.fare: Nothing new, ever. The same six dishes, in the same order, in the same bowls.
clues.fret: What the new girlfriend does over which fork, until an aunt waves it off.

clues.steamy: The lid comes off the pot and the kitchen window goes white all at once.
clues.yeast: The rolls have been rising under a dish towel on top of the stove since nine.
clues.stay: Nobody leaves right when eating is over. You do it another hour, minimum.
clues.yams: Candied, in the orange dish, and that dish has never held anything else.
clues.seam: Runs down the middle of the cloth, right where the leaf goes into the table.
clues.stem: Glasses with one come down off the top shelf twice a year, and this is once.

clues.extras: Two card tables in the hallway, because the good one only holds eight.
clues.extra: The place setting she lays anyway, in case somebody's friend turns up hungry.
clues.ears: The children keep theirs open while pretending to be busy with the dog.
clues.tear: What the youngest lets go when she hears she is in the hallway again.
clues.teas: Two pitchers on the counter: the sweet one, and the one for your uncle's sugar.
clues.east: The window the table faces, so two o'clock light lands right on the cake dome.

clues.cinder: The bottom of the rolls, the one Sunday she let your uncle watch the oven.
clues.dine: The word she uses on the phone, and she means two o'clock, not two-fifteen.
clues.rice: Under the gravy, and there is one correct ratio, decided long before you.
clues.cried: The baby, straight through grace, and not one eye opened early to look.
clues.iced: The cake got its coat on Friday and has been sitting untouched under glass.
clues.ride: Who collects your great-aunt is settled by Thursday, in the family group text.

clues.pricey: The roast she buys anyway, every single week, and never says what it ran.
clues.price: What the ham cost. Announced by nobody, guessed at by everybody at the table.
clues.pry: The aunts start in on your love life before the plates are even cleared.
clues.icy: The look that crosses the table the second somebody brings up the house.
clues.rye: Granddaddy's bottle, over the refrigerator, poured once the children go outside.
clues.ripe: She thumbed every peach in the bin Saturday for the cobbler, and put four back.

clues.castle: The dining room is hers the way one belongs to somebody: she says who enters.
clues.lace: The tablecloth edge, gone the color of weak tea, pressed every Saturday anyway.
clues.late: Arriving that way gets remembered, discussed, and brought up again next week.
clues.salt: On the table already. Reaching for it before you taste is the unforgivable one.
clues.tales: Told once the plates are pushed back, and the third version is always the best.
clues.slate: Wiped clean here. Whatever Friday was does not get to come to this table.

clues.hasten: Nobody does. Four hours at that table, and leaving early is a thing people note.
clues.nest: The napkins folded into the water glasses like something is meant to hatch.
clues.than: There is no better cook in this family, and saying it out loud starts something.
clues.neat: How the table gets set the night before: forks squared, chairs pushed in.
clues.tens: Two of them, folded, pressed into each grandchild's hand on the way out.
clues.heat: The rolls go back in for five minutes because your uncle finally turned up.

clues.enrich: What one covered plate from her kitchen does to a whole week of your lunches.
clues.rich: The macaroni is. Nobody asks how much cheese, and nobody wants the number.
clues.heir: Who gets the china is settled: she wrote it on a card taped inside the cabinet.
clues.chin: The youngest wears his dessert on his, and an aunt has the napkin out already.
clues.inch: What she has never given on the seating, no matter who asks to switch.
clues.rein: What she keeps on the conversation the second anybody starts in on politics.

clues.honest: What the Uptown album promised in its title, in a voice already sanded rough at twenty-one.
clues.notes: Four-part stack, and the lowest man is holding the one nobody in the car can hum.
clues.stone: What the sisters' harmony sits on: one held organ chord, unmoving under all of it.
clues.host: She reads the countdown Sunday night and calls number one before the ad break.
clues.shoe: Suede, brushed twice, worn to the video shoot and never once after.
clues.tens: What the tape counter reads at the ad-lib, and she rewinds to it every time.

clues.mentor: The producer who put her group on a B-side first, then let them keep the publishing.
clues.metro: Three rooms over a Philadelphia subway grate; the walls shook when the express came.
clues.tenor: He takes the second line in the quartet and the whole last verse by himself.
clues.term: Two albums and an option. What her lawyer struck through before anybody signed.
clues.omen: The first four bars of the drum program. You already know how the record ends.
clues.more: What the engineer wrote on the tape box next to the ad-lib pass: one again, louder.

clues.notice: Thirty days in writing before she walked from the label, taped to the studio door.
clues.tonic: Home key. The last chorus leaves it a whole step up and never comes back down.
clues.coin: Quarter in the diner jukebox slot, and she punches the slow one twice.
clues.cent: A penny a record after the split, which is what four of them each took home.
clues.icon: Her silhouette on the tour poster. Nobody prints the name because nobody has to.
clues.into: Where the ad-lib takes the final chorus: up and clear over the top of the choir.

clues.soften: What the compressor does to her breath so a whisper still sits over the bassline.
clues.often: Twice an hour after ten at night, until the request line finally stopped ringing.
clues.font: The label's gold script down the cassette spine, unreadable at arm's length.
clues.soft: How the ballad opens: brushed snare, no kick at all, until bar nine.
clues.sent: She mailed the four-track demo to A&R herself, no manager, return address in pen.
clues.tones: What the keyboard patch list calls them: bell, glass, and one just named Rhodes.

clues.stolen: Four bars nobody cleared in 1991, and the writer's daughter collected in court.
clues.stole: White fur over the gown at the awards, carried up the stairs like a robe.
clues.lens: What the director kept fogging for the rain scene, half the video budget gone.
clues.lone: One voice, no stack, no double: the a cappella eight bars the album opens on.
clues.sole: The writing credit, hers and nobody else's, on a record four men produced.
clues.lent: She gave the group her guide vocal for the demo and never got the tape back.

clues.ornate: The Atlanta label's cover art: gold leaf, heavy drape, four women shot like a painting.
clues.rate: Studio B by the hour, and the budget says finish the lead vocal before midnight.
clues.note: Held eight bars at the end while the band drops out from under her entirely.
clues.earn: What the four of them took in points instead of an advance, and it paid longer.
clues.tear: One down the cheek in the second verse, and the director kept that take.
clues.torn: The gym flyer off the pole, corner still taped, the DJ's name down at the bottom.

clues.townie: The one who stayed, and still knows which corner the group used to sing on.
clues.town: Population four thousand, one station, and it played her demo before anybody.
clues.twin: Two of the four are, and only one of them can hold the high harmony.
clues.nite: Spelled that way on the flyer because the club spelled it that way on the awning.
clues.wine: A cooler in the fridge for the anniversary; her tape runs longer than dinner.
clues.went: She left on the Greyhound with one cassette and came back with a deal.

clues.asking: What the post commander does over the mic at six: who still needs a perch plate?
clues.gains: What the relief fund shows after Friday, in the treasurer's hand, two columns, no calculator.
clues.sign: Poster board by the coat rack: PERCH $14, RYE BREAD, POTATO PANCAKES, FRIDAYS ONLY.
clues.sink: The three-tub washup by the walk-in. Her daughter runs it and keeps everybody moving.
clues.snag: A hitch, like the license copy nobody can find twenty minutes before doors open.
clues.kin: Your people. They eat first only if they worked the line, and never otherwise.

clues.whales: What the lodge quietly calls the big buyers: the man who takes forty boxes to his garage.
clues.slaw: Between the two slices of white bread, and if you say no she puts it on anyway.
clues.sale: What the shoe-polish lettering in the lodge window announces, repainted every month.
clues.wash: What the paper towels never quite do to your hands after breading forty pounds of lake trout.
clues.laws: The liquor board's rules, which the trustee can recite, and does, at every meeting.
clues.heals: What the lodge fund does for a member's light bill, quietly, and nobody names names.

clues.anchor: What the hall is for this stretch of the river. Catfish money, and it stays with the local.
clues.ranch: The dressing the young hands want in a cup. The retirees pretend not to hear them.
clues.horn: The yard blast at three-thirty. Twenty minutes later there are eighty boxes on the table.
clues.arch: Where the line bends around the flagpole once the second shift lets out.
clues.can: Tin of pickled peppers on every table. The steward's wife buys them by the flat.
clues.car: Where half the boxes end up, engine running, double-parked along the fence.

clues.hamlet: Four hundred people, one blinking light, and a township hall that seats ninety on a good night.
clues.metal: The folding tables, the fry baskets, the ash bucket by the door: all of it cold to the touch.
clues.math: The clerk's arithmetic at nine o'clock, done twice, and she does not want help with it.
clues.malt: In the cooler behind the bar, two dollars, and the license is taped up above it.
clues.heat: What comes off the two fryers by seven, and why the back door stays propped in February.
clues.tale: The one about the year the walleye did not come, told by a man who was not there.

clues.measly: What the alderman's check looked like beside what the block club raised in one night.
clues.yams: Candied, in a foil half-pan, brought by a woman who has voted in every primary since 1972.
clues.easy: How he thought the endorsement would come. She let him stand in the line like everybody.
clues.lays: What she does with the precinct map on the table once the plates are cleared away.
clues.same: The rented hall, the folding chairs, the speech: identical to two years ago.
clues.sly: How he works the room, shaking hands down the whole line without buying a plate.

clues.legion: Post 47. The bar in front, the fryers in back, and the cod comes in on Thursday.
clues.lingo: The talk in this hall: cases, shifts, ranks. Nobody explains it and nobody has to.
clues.long: How the wait runs after five, out past the pool table and into the parking lot.
clues.lion: The other club in town, the one that does chicken, which everybody insists is worse.
clues.leg: The bad one that keeps him on the register instead of the fryer. He still shows up.
clues.gone: What the last twelve dinners are by six-fifteen, and the adjutant tells you so herself.

clues.flames: What the company answers pages for, and what the fryer is not permitted to make in the bay.
clues.false: The alarm that pulled four of them off the line at six-forty, dinners still boxed.
clues.safe: The little one in the chief's office where the night's money sleeps until Monday.
clues.self: Take the rolls on your own. That end of the table is unstaffed and always has been.
clues.fame: What the haddock has across three towns, which is why cars line up at four-thirty.
clues.slam: The bay door dropping at eight. That is the sound of the night being over.

clues.fished: What half the hall did all summer, and what the lot smells like every Friday in Lent.
clues.dish: The pierogi pan the ladies bring covered and carry home washed, every single week.
clues.shed: Out back, where the folding tables and the six-foot hoagie trays wait all year.
clues.side: Pierogi or haluski, pick one, and the woman with the tongs will not let you take both.
clues.hide: What the last cod sandwich cannot do from the man who has been in line since four.
clues.dies: What the noise in the hall does the minute the Grand Knight's wife takes the microphone.
